title: Machine learning guides yeast alcohol dehydrogenase specificity for trans-2-nonenal
summary: Researchers measured a training library of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I variants, used support-vector activity regression/classification and a thermostability model to rank combinations, then tested 22 prioritized variants. Four showed higher specific activity toward trans-2-nonenal than wild type; LWFMY also showed improved thermostability under the study’s tests. The result is laboratory enzyme engineering, not an industrial process or validated product. The primary journal version was published 2026-11-01; a search result for an earlier-hosted copy had ambiguous date/provenance, so this entry does not claim it was the first public version.
ai_technology: Support-vector regression/classification models and docking-informed mutation selection
organization: RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science; Graduate School of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Kobe University

source_review.scope: Primary Springer full article and PubMed metadata; methods, dates, affiliations and outcomes.

evidence.tested: The top 22 ranked variants were experimentally evaluated; four outperformed wild type on trans-2-nonenal, with one also improved in thermal stability.
evidence.unknown: Small selected validation set; specific activity differs from catalytic efficiency across substrate concentrations; ambiguous earlier-hosted copy means first-public date is not asserted.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on measured variant data ranked combinations in unexplored sequence space for experimental testing.
